hypothesis: Blind geothermal faults concentrate at structural positions near catalogue-adjacent geophysical anomalies. Placing binary dots on catalogue-proximal zones (0-5px) weighted by multi-physics consensus surface captures withheld fault segments better than diffuse ridge-dot patterns.
mechanism: Multi-category consensus surface (magnetic, gravity, topographic, strain, seismic at 300m LoG scale) weighted by inverse distance to catalogue faults. Binary dots placed in near-fault zones (45% on-fault, 30% at 1px, 15% at 3px, 10% at 5px) with geophysical surface ranking. Differs from historical ridge-dot submissions by concentrating dots near catalogue traces rather than along linear ridges.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Unfaulted lithologic contacts, intrusive margins, or sedimentary facies changes can produce geophysical edges near catalogue faults without being faults.

holdout_dti.note: Pooled DTI alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, 300m triangular kernel. Proxy truth = withheld catalogue segments, not organizer labels.

feature_canary.note: All 20 tested features alone have holdout DTI < 0.02 (leakage threshold = 0.90). No single-feature leakage detected.

uniqueness.note: Spatial pattern differs fundamentally from historical ridge-dot submissions: dots concentrated near catalogue faults vs spread along linear ridges.
